That indicates that all Council members have to perform their duties impartially. And the test is that an objective, reasonable observer would conclude that the Council member can exercise their duties objectively without any undue influence. And then if there was a conflict of interest, the obligation of any member is to refuse to participate in the discussion and not to vote on the matter. And then I looked at, I think, two cases from other integrity commissioners to look at how these sorts of non-pecuniary conflicts of interest have been addressed in other circumstances. The reports and the codes of conduct in those two decisions were similar enough that I found that they were applicable here. And so what I considered based on those cases and your particular code is that the test was, is his personal feelings towards this particular contract employee so related to the decision that an independent, but a person who was well-informed of the history and the facts could come to the conclusion that it's more likely than not that that personal history would influence the Council member's decision-making on this particular decision.
